lesson.title: Reading 2D Lists
lesson.driving_question: How can a list of rows organise related fields into records?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Representing records as row lists and reading rows or cells
lesson.concept_budget: Read complete rows and individual cells from a fixed 2D list; data changes are deferred.
misconceptions: Each outer-list item is a complete row list.
The first index chooses a row.
The second index chooses a field inside that row.
Both row and column positions start at 0.
lesson.progression_note: Begins the Grade 8 data strand by extending familiar 1D indexing to records with rows and columns.

shared_program.code:
clubs = [["Art", 12], ["Chess", 18], ["Code", 15]]
row = int(input("Club row 0 to 2: "))
print("Record:", clubs[row])
print("Club:", clubs[row][0])
print("Members:", clubs[row][1])

primm.prompt: Recall how a position reads one item from a 1D list. In a record, what might a second position select?
Use row 1. Identify the complete selected row, then trace column 0 and column 1.
Run with row 1 and then row 0. Confirm that the first index changes the record while column meanings stay fixed.

questions: Why does clubs[1][0] select a field but clubs[1] selects a complete row?
What happens if the selected row position does not exist?
Why must every row keep the same field order for column 1 to mean members?
If you enter row 1, what record, club and member count are displayed?

primm.prompt: Add a second input for a valid column, 0 or 1. Display the selected field using clubs[row][column]. Test row 2 and column 0; it must display Selected field: Code.

Use a for loop to visit each row in [clubs]. For each [club], display "Club:" followed by the value at position 0, then display "Members:" followed by the value at position 1. The starter data must display Art with 12 members, Chess with 18 members and Code with 15 members without displaying list brackets.

Store ["Maths", 12], ["Music", 4] and ["Science", 8] in [timetable]. Ask for a row from 0 to 2 and store it in [row]. Display "Selected:" followed by the subject, "in room", and the room number from that row. Then use a for loop to display every subject name beneath "Subjects:". Test row 1; display "Selected: Music in room 4", followed by Maths, Music and Science on separate lines.
Repair the row brackets and use two square-bracket indexes to read the member count.

blocks.definition: A list whose items are row lists.

programs.challenge1:
clubs = [["Art", 12], ["Chess", 18], ["Code", 15]]
row = int(input("Club row 0 to 2: "))
column = int(input("Column 0 to 1: "))

print("Selected field:", clubs[row][column])
print("Record:", clubs[row])
print("Club:", clubs[row][0])
print("Members:", clubs[row][1])
programs.challenge2:
clubs = [["Art", 12], ["Chess", 18], ["Code", 15]]
for club in clubs:
    print("Club:", club[0])
    print("Members:", club[1])
programs.challenge3:
timetable = [["Maths", 12], ["Music", 4], ["Science", 8]]
row = int(input("Lesson row 0 to 2: "))
print("Selected:", timetable[row][0], "in room", timetable[row][1])
print("Subjects:")
for lesson in timetable:
    print(lesson[0])
